shots.composition_notes: Single locked-off wide-medium two-shot for the entire scene, camera never moves or cuts across all sampled frames. Husband (stop-motion figure with elongated nose) sits screen-left in profile/three-quarter view, wife sits screen-right at the kitchen island; both are framed roughly symmetrically at similar distance from camera, facing each other across the counter rather than toward the lens. Kitchen set fills the whole background (window screen-left, stove/cabinets center, dish rack and fridge edge screen-right), giving an eye-level, slightly low camera height that shows full cabinetry and hanging pendant lights above their heads with generous headroom. Coffee cups and open magazine on the counter sit in the lower-third foreground. Title/caption text is burned in center-low, overlapping the counter edge, and does not affect framing of the characters.

Full-frame black title card ("LOW BATTERY PEOPLE / CREATED BY NIN.") with centered stacked text and a small yellow 'NEW EPISODE DAILY' ticket graphic below; no live-action framing, pure static graphic card.
Single-frame flash/transition card: same title text on a plain white background, centered horizontally in the upper-middle of frame, functioning as a quick end-card flash rather than a composed shot.

framing_patterns_notes: The entire dialogue scene is shot as one unbroken static wide/medium two-shot with no coverage, no cuts to close-ups on reactions or punchlines, and no camera movement (pan/tilt/zoom) despite the scene running 14+ seconds with an escalating exchange ("emotional" / "me?" / "about" / "night") — all comedic beats are carried by puppet posing and dialogue timing rather than reframing. The video ends on two brief static graphic/title cards (black-background full title, then a white-background flash) rather than any additional live-action shot.
